claims.text: TC4 is a Ti6Al4V alloy with an unmodified alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
Unmodified TC4 has relatively low surface hardness.
Unmodified TC4 exhibits high wear rates under high-contact-stress conditions.
TC4 should be plasma nitrided at approximately 600 degrees Celsius or below.
Low-temperature plasma nitriding forms a thin, continuous, nitrogen-enriched surface layer on TC4.
The nitrogen-enriched layer contains TiN and/or Ti2N.
During plasma nitriding, nitrogen diffuses into the TC4 surface and reacts with titanium.
The resulting titanium nitride phases increase resistance to surface plastic deformation and abrasion.
Processing TC4 at approximately 600 degrees Celsius or below avoids alteration of its bulk microstructure.
Low-temperature plasma nitriding leaves the substrate's lightweight and alpha-plus-beta dual-phase properties intact.
Plasma-nitrided TC4 will have significantly greater surface hardness than untreated TC4.
Plasma-nitrided TC4 will have a lower wear rate than untreated TC4 under comparable test conditions.
Plasma nitriding will preserve the bulk ductility and toughness of TC4.
Plasma nitriding will preserve the corrosion resistance of TC4.
The improvement applies under ambient or moderately elevated temperatures and high-contact or sliding-wear conditions.
Performance may change when operating temperatures exceed the temperature capability of the nitride layer.
The magnitude and reproducibility of the improvement depend on nitriding temperature, duration, nitrogen flow, and service conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if treated samples fail to show a statistically significant hardness increase and corresponding wear-rate reduction relative to untreated controls.
The hypothesis is also falsified if TiN/Ti2N is absent or the nitride layer delaminates during testing.
